official.description: LSE offers LSE PhD Studentships to new PhD students alongside LSE DTP ESRC Studentships. The awards are open to high calibre students of all nationalities studying across all research areas at the School, are tenable for four years, and cover full fees and an annual stipend of GBP 23,805 with annual renewal subject to satisfactory academic performance.
official.english_requirement: MPhil/PhD programmes (except Law and Statistics) require the Research level for 2027/8 entry: IELTS (Academic) 7.0 overall (7.0 reading, 6.5 listening, 7.0 writing, 6.5 speaking) or TOEFL iBT 100 (25 reading, 22 listening, 27 writing, 22 speaking); Law PhD programmes require IELTS 7.5 overall. Tests must be less than two years old on 1 October 2027. Nationals and residents of listed majority English-speaking countries, or holders of a qualifying degree from one, are exempt.

applicant_utility.summary: This studentship pays full PhD fees plus a GBP 23,805 annual stipend for four years, but you never apply for it directly - your department nominates you from your PhD admission application, so the admissions file is the scholarship application. The decisive date is your department's first funding deadline for 2027/28 entry: complete applications with both references in by 3 December 2026 or 13 January 2027 are guaranteed consideration, while later candidates only compete for unawarded funds at the 27 May 2027 round. Apply as soon as the cycle opens in October 2026, because competition is intense and a late file can lose funding consideration entirely.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving graduates with a sharp research proposal that matches an LSE department's expertise, including international applicants who need full fees and living support.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your department's exact funding deadline on its programme page (some set 3 December 2026, others use 13 January 2027)
Contact a potential supervisor early where the department encourages it - supervisor fit drives the merit decision
Draft a research proposal of around 1,500 words and a 2-3 page statement of academic purpose
Nominate two referees early and chase them; the application is not considered until both references arrive
Book IELTS Academic or TOEFL early - Research-level scores for most MPhil/PhD programmes, higher in some departments, and tests must be under two years old at 1 October 2027
Submit as early in the cycle as possible once applications open in October 2026
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete application at the departmental funding deadline - usually a missing reference or transcript - which kills funding eligibility even if the academic place survives
A research topic with no matching supervisor or research group in the department
Missing the first funding panel and expecting an initial LSE PhD Studentship from the second round
Because there is no separate application, a thin admissions file leaves nothing else to rescue the funding case
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The studentship publishes full fees plus the GBP 23,805 stipend only; visa fees, the immigration health surcharge, flights to London, and any living or accommodation costs above the stipend remain self-funded.
document_audit: References must come from the referees you nominate in the system - documents sent directly to departments delay consideration
Only one online application is accepted per admissions cycle (October 2026 to September 2027); a second submission in the same cycle is not considered
Add GRE/GMAT only where the programme requires it - LSE warns selectors will not read extra documents
Some departments set their own proposal format or word count, so check the departmental guidance before finalising
alerts: Some departments set the 3 December 2026 early deadline and a few only submit to earlier funding panels
ESRC DTP consideration requires applying by your department's first funding panel deadline (3 December or 13 January 2027)
27 May 2027 is both the final funding deadline and the final application deadline - nothing new is accepted after it
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online admissions application with documents and referees, the department nominates you to the School funding panel, and the outcome arrives with your admissions decision.

applicant_utility.summary: The LSE Excellence Scholarship is a GBP 20,000 award for taught master's students in 13 named departments, split as GBP 10,000 per year on two-year programmes, and it needs no separate application because awardees are identified from the admissions pool. Allocation is rolling and ends without notice once the fund is exhausted, so the practical deadline is how early you submit rather than any published date. LSE publishes no breakdown of what the money pays for, so treat it as a partial contribution toward a costly London master's, not full funding.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong applicants to eligible-department master's programmes who want a merit award without preparing a separate funding application.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme sits in one of the 13 eligible departments before counting on this award
Submit the admission application early in the 2027/28 cycle, which opens in October 2026, because rolling allocation can end at any time
For double degree programmes, confirm the first year of study is at LSE
Exclude executive education programmes from consideration
Build a funding gap plan for remaining fees and London living costs
common_rejection_risks: Applying in a department outside the published list - for example Economics, Finance, Management and several others are not listed
Applying late in the cycle after all awards have been allocated
Double degree applicants whose first year of study is not at LSE
Treating the award as full funding and arriving with no backup for fees and living costs
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: LSE publishes no breakdown of what the GBP 20,000 pays for, so applicants should assume most tuition and all or most London living costs remain self-funded.
document_audit: The scholarship rides entirely on the admission application, so the statement of academic purpose and references are effectively the scholarship assessment
Applications are not considered until all supporting documents and both nominated references have arrived
Only one online application per admissions cycle; later programme changes go through the Graduate Applicant Portal and can cause delays
alerts: The published page still describes the 2026-entry round and LSE's scholarship overview states applications have closed for 2026 entry - watch for the updated 2027-entry page from October 2026
Rolling allocation means the fund can be fully committed with no further public notice
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one admission application for an eligible postgraduate taught programme; LSE identifies awardees from that application on a rolling basis and only contacts successful applicants.
